items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 23:1
items.html: The Galgalta of Arich Anpin is the stature of the male in its head, and the Sealed Brain is the stature of the female in the head, as in Answer 15 above; see there. And all the illuminations in the head come from the Galgalta, as it is the highest aspect in the head, and the smaller one beneath it, which is the Sealed Brain, does not ascend there in name. Only, the Galgalta itself is divided into two heads — the Galgalta and the Avir — and the place covered with hairs is called the Galgalta, while from the forehead and below, namely the twelve corrections of the face, the parts without hairs, are from the aspect of Mocha deAvira, as in Answer 22 above, see there. Yet in terms of the two heads, the corrections of the face are also called by the name of the Galgalta. (Page 318, Item 55; Page 308, Items 30-31).
